questions.q: Why does this report use DAX measures instead of dragging the TotalSalesAmount column straight onto a KPI card?
options: Power BI does not allow raw columns on KPI cards
DAX measures are required for every Power BI report regardless of content
Measures recalculate correctly as filters (like a future category slicer) change, which a raw column only mimics by coincidence here
Measures are always faster to compute than raw columns
questions.explain: A raw column works today only because the data is already aggregated; a measure is the habit that keeps working once filters or a bigger model are involved.

questions.q: Why does the Order Count measure use SUM instead of DISTINCTCOUNT?
options: The column is text, and SUM is required for text columns
OrderCount is already a column of pre-counted numbers from the T-SQL COUNT(DISTINCT...), so summing those numbers gives the correct total
SUM is always preferred over DISTINCTCOUNT for performance reasons
DISTINCTCOUNT is not a valid DAX function
questions.explain: The counting already happened in T-SQL; DISTINCTCOUNT on this column would count how many distinct order-count values exist, which is meaningless.

questions.q: What does the Average Order Value measure's formula look like?
options: AVERAGE(CategoryPerformanceSnapshot[TotalSalesAmount])
[Total Sales] / COUNTROWS(CategoryPerformanceSnapshot)
DIVIDE([Total Sales], [Order Count])
SUM([Total Sales]) / SUM([Order Count])
questions.explain: It references the two measures already built, Total Sales and Order Count, through DIVIDE rather than a raw column calculation.

questions.q: Why is DIVIDE used instead of a plain / operator in Average Order Value?
options: DIVIDE runs the calculation on the SQL Server instead of in Power BI
DIVIDE returns blank instead of raising a division-by-zero error if Order Count is ever zero for a filtered category
DIVIDE is required whenever two measures reference each other
The / operator does not exist in DAX
questions.explain: Once a slicer exists, a filtered category could have zero orders; DIVIDE handles that safely by returning blank instead of erroring.

questions.q: Where should these three measures be created?
options: In a separate Excel workbook linked to the report
As additional columns added to the Lesson 3 T-SQL query
In the Power BI model itself, as DAX measures -- not baked into the T-SQL query and not as calculated columns
As calculated columns on the CategoryPerformanceSnapshot table
questions.explain: Measures live in the model so they can be reused across the KPI cards, bar chart, and table without duplicating logic anywhere.
